headlines.title: Steph Curry avoids injury scare after hobbling out of Warriors open practice
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO – Warriors superstar Steph Curry avoided a serious injury scare Sunday that had thousands of fans holding their breath at Chase Center. Sunday was the Warriors’ open practice, where fans flock to get a look at their favorite players in a relaxed environment. The Warriors went a little more intense than in years past but still kept it light. About 45 minutes in, there was a heaviness of a dark cloud hovering over the court when Curry limped his way to the locker room. Curry went to make a move on De’Anthony Melton when his sneakers squeaked and his body got stuck. He tapped Melton, bounced the ball hard twice and favored his right leg limping to the sidelines. Curry caught his breath and then kept limping down the hallway and to the Warriors’ locker room. The main concern was that Curry, 38, injured the same right knee that held him out for more than two months last season. Luckily for Curry and the Warriors, that doesn’t appear to be the case. Curry has a sprained right ankle, per the Warriors, and did not injure his knee. “He said he’s fine,” Warriors coach Steve Kerr said after practice. Kerr shared that he spoke with Curry in the training room and that he was in good spirits. No further diagnosis has been shared, nor has a conversation with the Warriors’ medical staff. Like everybody in the building, Kerr certainly was worried for the worst when he first saw Curry in discomfort and admitted his heart skipped a beat. “Always, always,” Kerr said. “He’s fine. I went and talked to him after he went downstairs, and I went in the training room. He’s doing fine.” The Warriors have been cautious in Curry’s ramp-up leading to Wednesday’s regular-season opener in Los Angeles against the Los Angeles Lakers. Less is more in making sure Curry is as healthy as possible entering his 18th season. He has scrimmaged less and has been part of fewer and fewer higher-intensity portions of practice. Curry played a little under 18 minutes per game in the preseason and averaged 13 points while shooting 44 percent from the field (20 of 45) and 41.9 percent from three (13 of 31). Gui Santos was on the floor when Curry came up short, but his fear wasn’t at an all-time high because of his teammate’s reaction. “Of course we were scared,” Santos said. “But it’s Steph. He’s tough. He’s going to be good. Tomorrow he’s going to wake up and be good. We were definitely worried. … The way that I saw him walking off the court, I didn’t think it was something really bad.” The Warriors already are being tested from a plethora of health problems. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody continue to rehab leg injuries, and an illness has kept Kristaps Porziņģis away from the team for the last three weeks. Curry wasn’t the only concern from Sunday’s open practice, too. Brandin Podziemski and Charles Bassey did not participate. Bassey was seen having his right knee wrapped in ice, and the Warriors are saying he’s dealing with right knee tendinitis. Kerr did not know why Podziemski was absent but did confirm he practiced prior to the open session. Now, it’s another game of wait and see on Curry’s health days before the regular season begins. headlines.title: Driver arrested after hit-and-run crash seriously injures 2 children in Half Moon Bay
headlines.description: A driver who allegedly fled the scene of a Half Moon Bay collision that seriously injured two 6-year-olds was arrested Saturday night on multiple charges, according to the San Mateo County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the area of Grandview Boulevard and Golden Gate Avenue at approximately 5:45 p.m. Saturday following a report of a crash. Investigators learned that a vehicle struck two 6-year-olds who were riding bicycles before the driver fled the area. The two children sustained serious injuries and were transported to a hospital, where they were listed in stable condition. A witness who saw the collision provided deputies with a description of the driver and vehicle. Following an extensive search, deputies located the vehicle and — with assistance from the Daly City Police Department’s Drone Unit — found the suspect, 37-year-old Robert Schumann of San Francisco, hiding in a wooded area south of Bancroft Avenue. Investigators found evidence that Schumann was under the influence of alcohol. He was booked into the Maguire Correctional Facility on charges including suspected driving under the influence causing bodily injury, hit-and-run resulting in injury, driving with a suspended license due to a DUI conviction, and operating a vehicle with a blood-alcohol concentration over .01 while on probation. His vehicle was towed and impounded. Anyone with information is asked to contact the sheriff’s office at 650-363-4911, with anonymous tips accepted at 1-800-547-2700.

headlines.title: Small plane crashes into San Jose traffic; no serious injuries
headlines.description: A small plane carrying three people nosedived into traffic on one of San Jose’s busiest streets Saturday afternoon, leaving everyone aboard and on the ground with only non-life-threatening injuries. The crash occurred just before 3:10 p.m. at the intersection of Capitol Expressway and Excalibur Drive, blocking traffic, causing a minor fuel spill that crews quickly absorbed, and forced the Alum Rock Avenue off-ramp from Highway 680 to briefly shut down. Emergency responders from the San Jose Fire Department confirmed that two adults and a child were inside the aircraft — identified by Federal Aviation Administration records as a 1968 Cessna 177A Cardinal — when it went down, ending up nose-down and tail-up in the middle of the road. The three occupants were transported to a hospital out of an abundance of caution. No vehicles or individuals on the ground were struck or injured. Witnesses in the neighborhood expressed shock at finding a plane crash-landed just yards away from their homes. “It’s a close call, it’s a close call,” said Ricardo Barlaan of San Jose. Andrew Vasquez, another witness, recalled hearing the impact. Describing the moment, he made a crashing sound and said, “Boom.” “It’s crazy, I’m flabbergasted,” Vasquez said. “At first I thought it was some kind of stunt or they were making a movie or something.” Joe Lopez, who has lived in the neighborhood for 60 years, noted that while there have been past incidents involving aircraft flying out of nearby Reid-Hillview Airport, he had never seen a plane come down this close to his house. “It’s a good thing the navigator landed where he did,” Lopez said. The plane’s tail number indicates it is registered to Flying Twenty Inc., a nonprofit flight club for San Jose State University students, alumni, and faculty. According to the club’s website, they operate out of Reid-Hillview Airport. A club member reached by phone declined to comment about the organization, the pilot or what happened. It took about three hours before the wreckage was cleared from the intersection, carried away on a flatbed truck with a police escort — leaving a crumpled reminder of a crash that started with a mayday and ended with what emergency personnel called a miraculous survival story. Saturday’s incident highlights ongoing local safety concerns, marking the latest in a series of off-airport aircraft accidents tied to facilities in East San Jose. According to National Transportation Safety Board records and published news reports, several similar off-airport crashes have occurred over the decades: Feb. 24, 2002: A Piper PA-24-250 lost engine power due to fuel exhaustion while approaching Reid-Hillview Airport, forcing the pilot to make an emergency street landing about two miles away where it collided with a car. The NTSB attributed the crash to inadequate flight planning and improper fuel-consumption calculations. No injuries were reported. Nov. 19, 2017: CBS reported that a Cessna 172P suffered a partial engine power loss after taking off from Reid-Hillview Airport, crashing into a garage on Evelyn Avenue roughly 300 yards northwest of the property. While no one inside the residence was hurt, the pilot sustained minor injuries and two passengers suffered serious injuries. June 29: A small experimental gyrocopter with two people on board crashed just outside Reid-Hillview Airport near Eastridge Mall. One occupant was hospitalized with moderate injuries, while the other was evaluated at the scene for minor injuries, according to a report from Newsbreak.

headlines.title: Woman detained while walking on Hwy. 101 in San Jose dies
headlines.description: A woman seen walking on Highway 101 “with a knife” causing major traffic delays died after being taken to the hospital on Saturday, according to authorities. CHP said it received a call around 11:10 a.m. regarding a woman walking near Highway 101, just south of Bernal Road. Authorities said the initial report indicated she was walking from the right-hand shoulder toward the center divide. At 11:13 a.m., CHP said the woman was reportedly “going after vehicles with a knife.” However, San Jose police later said an on-duty sergeant saw her “actively injuring herself.” The woman was taken into custody by police and taken to a local hospital, where she died, according to the police department. The incident caused major delays on Highway 101. CHP said lanes 1 and 2 reopened on southbound 101, just south of Highway 85, at 11:43 a.m.

headlines.title: Valkyries win WNBA Finals Game 1 against the Dream amid Ballhalla's roaring cheers
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries won 68 to 64 against the Atlanta Dream on Saturday afternoon during Game 1 of the WNBA Finals. The game took place in San Francisco, at the Valkyries’ home, Chase Center, which the team and fans refer to as “Ballhalla.” The game was close and had the 18,000 fans in attendance standing and cheering the whole way through. The Ballhalla fans, known for being extremely loud, somehow seemed even louder under the pressure and excitement of the league finals. Fans screamed with pure elation and danced in their seats at the final buzzer as violet streamers rained down on Chase Center. It is a day that will go down in Bay Area sports history because the Valkyries not only played their first WNBA Finals game, but also secured their first WNBA Finals win. In the Valkyries’ first season, they became the first WNBA expansion team to make the playoffs in their inaugural season. Now in season two, their playoff run has stretched even farther, and the team continues attaining major milestones. Saturday was the team’s 50th consecutive sold-out crowd. The team has sold out every single home game in its history so far. Valkyries fans said they got bit stressed by the end of the game, but were overjoyed to see their team lock in a win. “My blood pressure was way up during the game, especially during the fourth quarter,” said Rolinda Wang of San Francisco. “I knew they were going to pull it off, I just felt it. And I am so excited for them, and us.” Many fans, like 11-year-old Abigail Pulter of San Francisco, said the fans at this game seemed even louder and more energized than usual. “It’s such a great atmosphere, it’s amazing, especially for women’s sports,” Pulter said. “It’s a big hit and our first finals.” Pulter also described the visual of the crowd at the game all in Valkyries violet as “like a purple sea.” There were some big names in the crowd watching the Valkyries make history at Ballhalla. Bay Area singer Goapele performed the national anthem. Singer and actress Rita Moreno hit the drum to mark the start of the game. Bay Area rapper Larry June performed at halftime. A variety of members of the Golden State Warriors organization past and present also showed up to support the Valkyries, including Warriors Coach Steve Kerr, point guard Steph Curry, and forward Draymond Green. Fans spoke proudly about why they feel the Bay Area and the Valkyries team work so well together. “It’s a loving community all around, this is the spirit of the Bay, this is where we live, it represents the best of all of us,” said Nathan Good, who has befriended many people through Valkyries games. Game two of the Finals will be at Chase Center again on Monday evening. Fans said they are making plans to head to Ballhalla, Thrive City, or their favorite sports bars to watch.

headlines.title: Head-on crash leaves 1 person dead and 2 injured in San Jose
headlines.description: A person died and two others were injured following a head-on collision in San Jose Sunday morning, police said. Police said the collision was reported shortly before 6:30 a.m., near Capitol and McLaughlin avenues. Authorities said three people were taken to the hospital, where one person died. Authorities said this is an ongoing investigation.

headlines.title: Vacaville man killed after car veers off I-80, hits tree near Fairfield
headlines.description: A 23-year-old Vacaville man died early Sunday morning after his car veered off Interstate 80 and crashed into a tree near Fairfield, according to the California Highway Patrol. The CHP Golden Gate Communications Center received an automated iPhone crash notification at approximately 2:52 a.m. Sunday, reporting an incident on westbound I-80 near the Cordelia Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Facility scales. Solano Area CHP officers arrived at the scene at 3:01 a.m. and located a silver 2014 Hyundai Elantra that had struck a tree just west of the scales. The solo occupant was trapped in the driver’s seat, unresponsive, not breathing and without a pulse. Officers performed CPR until the Fairfield Fire Department arrived and extricated the driver. He was transported to NorthBay Medical Center in Fairfield, where he was pronounced dead at 3:27 a.m. A preliminary investigation indicates the Hyundai was traveling westbound when the driver allowed the vehicle to veer off the right side of the freeway for reasons still under investigation. Investigators believe the driver was not wearing a seatbelt. Alcohol is suspected to be a contributing factor, though official toxicology results are pending. The Solano County Coroner’s Office will release the man’s identity pending family notification. The CHP Solano Area is actively investigating the crash and urges witnesses to come forward.

headlines.title: Gabby Williams scores 26 points, sends Valkyries to 68-64 Game 1 win in defensive WNBA Finals opener
headlines.description: Gabby Williams converted two free throws with 1:18 left to put Golden State ahead, two more with 4.1 seconds to go and finished with 26 points facing constant pressure from Atlanta’s stingy defense, and the Valkyries held off the Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday. Williams scored 16 of her points in the second quarter and no other Valkyries reached double figures as they shot 32.1% and 7 of 33 from 3-point range. “We always knew we were going to find a way somehow,” Williams said on the microphone postgame as fans chanted “Gabby! Gabby!” Rhyne Howard missed a 3-point try with 1:09 left but Angel Reese made a steal moments later. Naz Hillmon missed from deep. Kiah Stokes missed the first of two free throws with 23.8 seconds left. Then Allisha Gray missed a 3 with 9 seconds left. Williams then hit the free throws a few seconds later to seal the victory. Game 2 in the best-of-seven series is Monday night back at Chase Center, where the ear-piercing noise from a raucous “Ballhalla” crowd made for the exact hostile environment Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase requested from the home fans. One of these two franchises will capture its first championship, and if the first game is any indication it’s going to be an all-out defensive fight. Gray returned from injury to score 19 points, Reese added 14 points and 12 rebounds. Jordin Canada contributed eight points, seven assists and five rebounds for the Dream, hitting a timely 13-foot jumper with 4:23 remaining. Williams’ driving layup with 3:22 to play pulled Golden State within 62-61. Canada banged awkwardly into Williams’ knee on a box out during her late free throws and the Valkyries star was being cared for by an athletic trainer on the bench in the waning moments. Gray was in the starting lineup and had gone through a light practice Friday after missing the last two games of Atlanta’s sweep of the New York Liberty in the best-of-three semifinal series with an injured left ring finger — on her shooting hand. Golden State guard Tiffany Hayes hit her face hard on the floor trying to make a steal in the closing minutes and was down with 2:38 remaining before walking off the court on her own to the locker room.

headlines.title: ‘No Kings' protest in San Francisco encourages early voting
headlines.description: Millions took the streets in cities across the country on Saturday for the fourth so-called “No Kings” protest. Dozens of Bay Area cities held rallies, with San Francisco holding one of the largest locally. The National Coalition said the events were meant to be nonpartisan and aimed to increase voter participation, but the crowds at most had a clear tilt against the current administration. The crowds were full of demonstrators carrying anti-Trump and No Kings signs, along with an atmosphere of a rolling block party. There was music and dancing, with organizers saying the focus was on voting rights and early voting. “Early voting matters in this political climate so much because you never know what is going to happen next, there is so much things popping up that is coming from the federal level or other areas that it is just safer to vote earlier. Also, you never know what is going to happen with yourself life happens with yourself and also the ballot is pretty long as you may have noticed,” Adam Sheehan with Indivisible San Francisco said. Some demonstrators here say their concern was on what’s happening other states as opposed to California, defending democracy and election integrity. Critics of these protests, including several Republicans, have denounced the rallies as staged and misguided in the past. They said organizers should be looking to bring people together rather than stoking division. Back at the rally, several demonstrators brought their completed ballots to drop off at an official drop box after the event, reinforcing their vote, and vote early message.

headlines.title: San Francisco police investigate homicide in Bayview District
headlines.description: The San Francisco Police Department is investigating a homicide in the Bayview District after they found a man suffering from a gunshot wound, police announced Saturday. According to the police, they responded to the 1100 block of Wisconsin Street regarding a shooting on Friday, at around 8:38 p.m. When they arrived, officers found a man suffering from an apparent gunshot wound. However, despite first aid and lifesaving efforts by paramedics, the victim succumbed to his wound and was pronounced deceased on scene, police said. Anyone with information is asked to call the SFPD 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD. You may remain anonymous.

headlines.title: Rep. DeSaulnier's Walnut Creek district office receives ‘suspicious envelope'
headlines.description: Congressman Mark DeSaulnier said a “suspicious envelope” was delivered to his Walnut Creek district office Friday afternoon. According to DeSaulnier, the U.S. Capitol Police reported that several congressional district offices have received “suspicious envelopes” containing “threatening letters and a white powdery substance.” He said the envelope delivered to his district office matched that description. The Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office said there was a “large presence” near DeSaulnier’s office. Here’s DeSaulnier’s full statement: “Following reports from U.S. Capitol Police of identical suspicious envelopes containing threatening letters and a white powdery substance that were delivered to other Congressional district offices across the nation, a member of our team identified a letter matching the description and return address, immediately secured the envelope without opening it, and called local law enforcement and U.S. Capitol Police. “Threats and political violence seem to have reached a fever pitch in our country, and I urge my fellow Americans to stand united against such attempts at undermining our democracy. “My priority remains the safety and security of my team, and I am thankful for the quick and decisive response. We remain committed to serving CA-10 residents and will not be deterred from this important work by threats.” The listed return address was a Manhattan location linked to the Democratic Socialists of America, but the group said they have not had offices there in years. Minority leader Chuck Schumer had a threatening letter intercepted, according to a spokesman. California Senator Alex Padilla says he was also alerted that his office was targeted. Local offices of several other elected leaders also received these letters. Representative Zoe Lofgren posted that law enforcement was immediately called after her San Jose office received a suspicious letter, adding that her staffers are safe and the investigation is ongoing. Representative Jimmy Panetta says staff opened an envelope Friday morning and realized there was powder inside. She immediately put the envelopes in the garbage can and cleared staff members out of the office and called 911. Law enforcement officials said initial testing of the envelope was negative. But experts say Capitol Hill police, the FBI and postal inspectors have to treat these letter threats seriously. “The impact could be deadly, because the one time that you’re wrong, you know innocent bystanders could end up, could end up deceased or very sick,” Former NJ FBI Director Timothy Gallagher said. These letters have now been sent nationwide, with some being delivered to state officers in Louisiana, Ohio and Oklahoma on Thursday. The mailings come three weeks before election day, and an investigation to track the sender could take some time.

headlines.title: Valkyries fans prepare for the team's historic debut in the WNBA Finals
headlines.description: Fans of the Golden State Valkyries are gearing up for a milestone event in Bay Area sports history: the Valkyries’ debut in the WNBA Finals. The team, which is only in its second year have garnered enormous support from fans for their culture on and off the court. Game one of their series against the Atlanta Dream will start at 12:30 p.m. Pacific in San Francisco at Chase Center. It is possible the series could run up to seven games depending on how long it takes a team to win four games. Even before the game started, fans have been proudly wearing their Valkyries gear around the Bay Area and planning out how they’ll watch the games. At Rikki’s, a sports bar in San Francisco’s Castro that prioritizes women’s sports, staff are preparing for what they will expect to be days of lines out the door when the finals are on. So far, the bar has been at capacity during the Valkyries post-season run, as fans look for chances to cheer on the team together. “This moment is something I think I hoped for but did not think would happen this fast, for this team to be this good and this kind of connected to the community,” said Danielle Thoe, a co-owner and general manager at Rikki’s. Thoe said the Valkyries have been very supportive of sports bars in their network, sending along freebies and team merch to watch parties. “I think the Valkyries are showing that like womens sports fandom has no limit,” Thoe said, adding that the Valkyries success comes at a time when momentum around women’s sports in the Bay Area is on the rise. The Valkyries have hit many milestones during their only two ears of existence. The team sold out every single home game they have played so far. Last year, they became the first WNBA expansion team to advance to the playoffs in their inaugural year. The team has also built a vibrant fanbase and now have a real shot at being league champions. “I cannot explain how much excitement I have inside and among everyone I know, the number of texts I am getting,” said Julie Dorf of Berkeley, a season ticket holder. “This is just one more really neat thing for the Bay Area, for the city, for California,” said Tracey McNamara of Mendocino County, who is in San Francisco to attend game one of the finals on Saturday. The Valkyries plan to have activities for fans outside Thrive City on game days. Sports bars across the Bay Area are planning watch parties for the finals as well.
